question: A team is choosing which slice of work to use for a two-week trial of a new Claude-assisted contract summarising arrangement. Which slice is the best choice for the trial?
options: A) The contracts causing the most delay right now, so the trial also clears the urgent backlog.
B) A random sample drawn from the whole archive, including contracts that are no longer in force.
C) A representative mix, including the awkward cases the team knows the arrangement must survive.
D) The simplest contracts, so the trial is not derailed by problems that affect only unusual cases.
correct_answers: C) A representative mix, including the awkward cases the team knows the arrangement must survive.
explanations: Using the trial to clear a backlog mixes two goals and puts urgent work in the hands of an untested arrangement. The most delayed contracts are also often the least typical, so they are a poor sample.
A random archive sample sounds rigorous but includes expired contracts the team no longer handles. Effort goes into cases that will never recur, and the awkward live cases may not appear at all.

Correct. A pilot is only useful if it is a fair rehearsal of the real work, which means deliberately including the hard cases. Two weeks on a representative mix shows both what the arrangement handles well and where it must keep a person involved.
An easy slice produces a flattering result that does not predict live performance. The arrangement would then meet its first difficult contract after the team has already committed to it.
